title: Resolution theorem: C_•(Φ, V) → V (Thm 7.1.7)
body_html:
Resolution theorem

Theorem (Sheaf7 Thm 7.1.7). Assume the compatible-system axioms (T1)–(T5) including in particular (T3) $G$-equivariance, the per-vertex acyclicity of $C_\bullet(\Phi, V)[\phi_x]$ (Acyclicity of C_d(Φ, V)[φ_x] for vertices x), and the Serre-subcategory hypothesis (S) (Serre-subcategory property (S) — a consequence, not a hypothesis). Then for every $V \in \Rep_\Phi(G)$, the augmented complex $$\cdots \to C_1(\Phi, V) \to C_0(\Phi, V) \xrightarrow{\epsilon_V} V \to 0$$ is exact, i.e.\ $C_\bullet(\Phi, V)$ is a resolution of $V$.

Note on hypothesis tightness. Of the (T·) axioms only (T3) is used directly in the assembly proof below; the per-vertex acyclicity lemma transitively uses the rest of (T1)–(T5) plus (K3), but those are isolated in that lemma's hypothesis box rather than restated here.
proof_html:
By (T3), every term of the augmented complex $\mathcal{C}_\bullet$ is generated by its $\phi_x$-isotypic components as $x$ ranges over vertices of $A$. Under (S), the homology $H_\bullet(\mathcal{C}_\bullet)$ lies in $\Rep_\Phi(G)$, hence is generated by $\bigcup_x H_\bullet[\phi_x]$. Taking $\phi_x$-isotypic component is exact, so it suffices to show $\mathcal{C}_\bullet[\phi_x]$ is acyclic — which is Acyclicity of C_d(Φ, V)[φ_x] for vertices x. $\square$

Remark. When $R = \mathbb{C}$ and $V$ has a central character, each $C_d(\Phi, V) = \bigoplus_\mathcal{F} \cInd_{\hat K_\mathcal{F}}^G V[\phi_\mathcal{F}]$ is projective in $\Rep_\Phi(G)$; the resolution is then projective, with all the standard homological algebra consequences.

This resolution is the prototype of the §7.4 localization and the heart of the §8 main theorem.
